# Library multiplayer fixture protocol

Start this fresh F200 world, then connect exactly two real clients whose actual `LuaPlayer.locale` values report `en` and `de`. Initial unchanged locales do not require a locale-change event. Wait for the `rejoin-ready` marker, disconnect and reconnect both clients, then wait for `restart-ready` and the requested `mir5-library-multiplayer-restart` save. Restart the host from that save, reconnect both clients again, and wait for `completed` plus `mir5-native-complete`.

The control requests eight GUI screenshots under `script-output/mir5-library-multiplayer/`: Availability, initial personal view, rejoin and host restart for each client. The initial Availability view contains exactly two terminal Space Age requirement explanations and stays open for 60 ticks before ordinary personal views replace it. Screenshots become rendering evidence only after external PNG readback confirms the files; a headless request is not a rendering result.

After the initial personal views are open, the fixture keeps their public browser root and query objects, marks only the four named science-pack prerequisites researched, and queues two real levels of `recipe-prod-research_gears-1`. Its fixture-local `settings-updates.lua` reduces only that stream’s count and time so two actual lab completions can be observed within the bounded disposable world; it does not qualify ordinary cost or time tuning. The lab receives two of each named pack, and the control requires public force queue lengths 2→1→0 plus native started/finished events, `by_script == false`, level three, the resulting +20% iron-gear-wheel productivity, and zero remaining packs before it preserves the post-lab snapshot.

The fixture then queues and cancels one third level through `LuaForce.cancel_current_research`, requiring the native cancellation callback and no third laboratory completion. It creates a separate foreign force and requires that its initial gear level/productivity and both already-open player views remain independent. It never imports MIR internals, reads MIR storage, or synthesizes native events. The unchanged rejoin and host-restart stages still verify the stored post-lab witness and all eight client-local captures.
